chapter: Suntaug Lake Inn and Duke Ellington's band
title: Song pluggers and his tunes stolen
summary: Whaley says tunes he made up, like 'Japanese Sandman', were taken by others, and that after he arrived in New York his arrangements were heard at the Savoy.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: We were talking about this place in Boston where you used to play, but you want to talk about some songs now.

Yeah, you see, all them guys used to come down and bring the lead sheet, the song pluggers and I used to try to get the guys interested in -- I had a song I said -- it goes like this (Humming) 'Japanese Sandman', see, I used to play that and didn't have a melody to it and I don't know how it got away from me, but first thing I know somebody come out with 'Japanese Sandman.' I said, man, I used to play that long while ago. And I got a number (humming) and no one stole that because it's too hard. Got somemore there. I used to write -- make up numbers and nothing happened until I came
here to New York and they started stealing all my music. The band would play in the theatre and the next week they'd be up the Savoy and you'd go up there that week and you hear my music up there.
